Few figures embody the fusion of pastoral devotion and unyielding moral courage quite like Wilhelm Finnemann, a German-born missionary whose life culminated in a heroic stand against wartime atrocities. Born on December 18, 1882, in the small village of Wietersheim, Germany, Finnemann entered the Society of the Divine Word (SVD) in 1901, a missionary congregation dedicated to spreading the Gospel in distant lands. Ordained a priest in 1909, he embarked on a path that would lead him to the Philippines, where his ministry would leave an indelible mark on the Church and the Filipino people.  

Finnemann's missionary zeal brought him to the archipelago in 1910, where he immersed himself in the cultural and spiritual fabric of Mindoro Island. Rising through the ranks, he served as a seminary rector and later as Prefect Apostolic of Mindoro, a role that demanded both administrative acumen and evangelical fervor. In 1937, Pope Pius XI consecrated him as the Titular Bishop of Sora and Auxiliary Bishop of Manila, a testament to his growing influence. Yet, it was not ecclesiastical titles that defined Finnemann but his proximity to the suffering faithful. He championed education, established schools, and advocated for the indigenous Mangyan people, fostering a Church rooted in social justice long before such concepts gained widespread currency.  

The shadow of World War II transformed Finnemann's episcopacy into a crucible of faith. When Japanese forces invaded the Philippines in December 1941, Mindoro fell under brutal occupation. Amid the chaos, Japanese soldiers began rounding up Filipina women for forced conscription into "comfort stations"—a euphemism for systematic sexual slavery. Finnemann, then 59 and frail from years of tropical hardships, refused to stand idle. From his residence in Calapan, he confronted the occupiers directly, hiding women in his home and issuing public denunciations that echoed the prophetic fire of biblical figures like Nathan rebuking David.  

His defiance proved fatal. On October 26, 1942—exactly 83 years ago as of this writing—Japanese troops arrested Finnemann on suspicion of aiding resistance fighters. Subjected to savage torture, including beatings and mock executions, the bishop remained steadfast, reportedly telling his captors, "I am ready to die for my faith and for the women of Mindoro." He was summarily executed by bayonet, his body left unburied as a grim warning. Eyewitness accounts from survivors paint a portrait of serene resolve: even in agony, Finnemann prayed aloud, forgiving his tormentors.  

Finnemann's martyrdom reverberated beyond the islands. In 1999, the Catholic Church formally recognized his cause for beatification, declaring him a Servant of God—the inaugural step toward sainthood. Today, his legacy endures in Mindoro's St. Joseph Cathedral, where his relics are venerated, and in the annual commemorations that honor his role as a shepherd who laid down his life for his flock.

$GRAB &"Relentless Innovation"- SEA Monopoly🧵

Grab Holdings Limited, Southeast Asia's preeminent SuperApp, has solidified its position as a multifaceted ecosystem serving over 46 million monthly transacting users across eight countries (Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam). As of Q2 2025, Grab reported record profitability with $819 million in revenue (up 23% YoY), $35 million in GAAP profit, and adjusted EBITDA of $109 million, fueled by 21% YoY on-demand GMV growth to approximately $5.5 billion. This performance underscores Grab's evolution from a 2012 ride-hailing startup to a dominant player contributing up to 1% of Thailand's GDP and 0.5% of Malaysia's.

Grab operates across four core segments: Deliveries, Mobility, Financial Services, and Others generating diversified revenue streams. In 2023, Deliveries accounted for 50.61% of total revenue, Mobility 36.8%, Financial Services ~8%, and Others (including advertising and enterprise) the balance. By Q1 2025, these segments drove 18% YoY revenue growth to $773 million, with broad-based gains: Deliveries up 19%, Mobility 27%, and Financial Services 53%. Grab's "relentless innovation" strategy emphasizing AI integration, hardware advancements, and ecosystem synergies that focuses on delivering superior value beyond mere pricing.

Grab has been dealing with price war since its inception, @AnthonyPY_Tan understood $GRAB has to embrace innovation and offer more value to maintain monopoly. This approach creates "stickiness" through convenience, personalization, and network effects, deterring low-price entrants like $SE/ShopeeFood or emerging local apps by raising the bar on user experience and loyalty. With $7.6 billion in cash (32% of market cap) , Grab is re-rating as a high-growth, profitable bet on the region's $1 Trillion billion digital economy by 2025. Grab does not deserve to trade at forward 2.7 P/S(2026). Short sellers are showing early sign of exiting, this may be an inflection point for investors.  

1. Deliveries:

Grab's Deliveries segment, encompassing food, grocery, and parcel services, is its largest by revenue and a key driver of daily user engagement. It connects over 2 million merchant partners with consumers via a seamless platform, processing 100 million+ monthly transactions. In Q1 2025, Deliveries revenue hit $415 million (up 19% YoY), with GMV growing 19% amid Ramadan demand surges, outpacing rivals like Gojek (down 10% YoY in 2023). Advertising within this segment surged 60% YoY to $176 million, diversifying income beyond commissions (15-30% take rates).

Core Op: 
~GrabFood: Dominant in food delivery (50%+ market share), offering 30-minute ETAs, diverse cuisines from 500,000+ restaurants, and contactless handover. It leverages GrabMaps for real-time routing, reducing delays in urban congestion.

~GrabMart: Grocery and essentials delivery, growing faster than food during peak periods like Ramadan; integrates with hyperlocal stores for same-hour fulfillment.

~GrabExpress: On-demand logistics for parcels, documents, and e-commerce, serving B2B and B2C with tracked, insured shipments.

Relentless Innovation: Grab counters low-price rivals ( ShopeeFood's subsidies) by emphasizing reliability and personalization, not just discounts. At the inaugural GrabX 2025 showcase, Grab launched AI-powered features under "For Every You," tailored to users. 
"Grab for family", "Group Order sharing", "Grab Smart food lockers", "Dine-Out", "Tourist Dining Bundles"... 

These innovations, powered by @awscloud  Inferentia chips for ML inference, process 200 TB of data daily, enabling predictive inventory and fraud detection. By focusing on "Secret Weapon"-"affordability" (Saver options at 20% lower fares without quality cuts), Grab expands to price-sensitive users while maintaining 75% market share. Grab Drone is also being tested, most likely to be scaled in 2026-2027 to hit 50-60% software like margin. 

2. Mobility

Mobility remains Grab's foundational segment, offering ride-hailing and shared transport to 700+ million in underserved areas. Q1 2025 revenue reached $282 million (up 27% YoY), with GMV at $1.815 billion (23% YoY), driven by 19% transaction growth and record driver supply. It holds 75%+ regional share(in many cities it is 90-95%), post-Uber's 2018 exit. As soon as $goto to go away or confiscated, $Grab will have 90-95% market share

Core Op: 
~GrabCar/GrabBike: Economy to premium rides (cars, bikes, taxis); dynamic pricing balances supply-demand.

~Shared Rides & Rentals: Carpooling and hourly rentals for efficiency in traffic-heavy cities like Manila.

~Enterprise Fleet: B2B shuttles for corporations, integrating with HR systems.

Relentless Innovation: Against low-cost disruptors ( Bolt-like entrants), Grab prioritizes safety and personalization via AI, reducing churn from poor experiences. GrabX 2025 emphasized "purpose-led" mobility. GrabUnlimited members will get as low fares as Bolt, with highest discounts on other services Grab offers. Some other additional features to offer higher value/safety for this segment:

"Advance Booking (Airport Pickup)", "Grab for Family", "GrabExecutive", "KartaCam 2 & KartaDongle", "Autonomous Vehicle Pilots"

These leverage Catwalk ML platform on AWS EKS for ETA predictions (50K requests/sec), focusing on "Saver Rides" for budget users (7% of rides, 213% YoY growth) without eroding premiums.

3. Financial Segment

GrabFin targets the 60%+ unbanked population, offering digital banking, payments, lending, and insurance. It's the fastest-growing segment, with Q1 2025 revenue at $74 million (up 38% YoY) and loans disbursed at $639 million (44% YoY). Deposits hit $1.2 billion, with annualized loan run-rate nearing $3 billion in Q2. 

Core Op:
~GrabPay: Wallet for seamless payments across ecosystem; QR codes for offline merchants.

~Lending & Insurance: Microloans to drivers/merchants; usage-based auto insurance.

~Digital Banks: GX Bank (Malaysia/Singapore) and partnerships (with Singtel).

Relentless Innovation:To fend off fintech upstarts ( SeaMoney's low-fee wallets), Grab embeds finance into daily life(daily interest, no minimum balance), using data for low-risk, high-value products:

"QR Payment Expansion", "AI Fraud Detection & Personalization", "GXS Bank Enhancements" 

Instant, no-balance payments; boosts unbanked access. Secure, instant approvals; 79% YoY loan book to $710M.High-yield savings + ecosystem rewards.
@AnthonyPY_Tan wants GrabFin to be default payment option in SEA and future expansion. 

4. Others:

This nascent segment (~5% revenue) includes advertising ($176M in Q1, +60% YoY), GrabMaps licensing, and new initiatives like e-commerce via Everrise acquisition. It powers cross-segment synergies,  targeted ads in Deliveries.

Core Op: 

~Advertising & Enterprise: Data-driven ads; B2B tools for fleets/merchants.

~GrabMaps: Proprietary mapping for internal/external use; $10B SEA market Long term.

~Other B2B products

~Telecom, Car rental and others. Low-cost Telecom will amplify MTUs, Grab could give out 1 month GrabUnlimited trial with GrabPoint to bring even more users to try its services

Relentless innovation: By adding more "affordable" services that are essential to SEA folks, $GRAB is well positioned to capture even more market share with higher penetration (currently at 6.5%)

5. Strategic Moat

Grab’s relentless innovation spanning AI-driven personalization, hardware like KartaCam, and tourism-focused bundles creates a formidable moat against low-price competitors. By integrating Deliveries, Mobility, Financial Services, and emerging ventures into a seamless superapp, Grab delivers unmatched convenience, capturing 84% user retention and 75%+ market share. 

The 2025 tourism expansion, targeting 152 million visitors, adds a high-margin growth vector: bundled ride + dining + ticketing services, multi-currency payments, and attraction partnerships make Grab indispensable for travelers, a segment low-cost apps can’t penetrate without comparable ecosystems. With $7.6 billion in cash balance sheet, $GRAB is ready to take more market share.

Conclusion: 

GRAB SuperApp exemplifies how strategic innovation can transform regional challenges like unbanked populations, urban congestion, and booming tourism into enduring competitive advantages. Its superapp model, fortified by AI, proprietary data (800B+ API calls/month), and a $7.6 billion war chest, creates a virtuous cycle of user loyalty and operational efficiency. The aggressive tourism push, capturing the 152 million visitor market with integrated travel solutions, cements Grab’s role as Southeast Asia’s digital gateway, outpacing price-driven rivals like ShopeeFood or Gojek. 

Short-term competitions may insist, but Grab’s 11 quarters of EBITDA gains, positive free cash flow, and SEA market consolidation signal robust fundamentals. 30%+ growth is locked in from Q4 2025, we should hear more updates on Q3 ER. More than half of tourists are using Grab, Anthony wants 80-90%, and he will get it. Grab's "relentless innovation" isn't just a buzzword; it's a core strategy to fend off rivals like Gojek, ShopeeFood, and global entrants. New players will start losing money on the very first transaction(high promo/free delivery), and that is unsustainable long term.
